{{nihongo|'''Arakashi Shrine'''|荒橿神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimotsuke Province]].

'''Arakashi Shrine''' (あらかしじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located at 325 Koido, {{ill|Motegi, Tochigi|Q644327|qid=Q644327}}, {{ill|Haga District, Tochigi|Q1192087|qid=Q1192087}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|qid=Q44843}}. It is identified with the “Arakashi Shrine” of Haga District, {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ca|Província de Shimotsuke|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆتسوکی|cs|Provincie Šimocuke|de|Provinz Shimotsuke|es|Provincia de Shimotsuke|fa|ولایت شیموتسوکه|fr|Province de Shimotsuke|gl|Provincia de Shimotsuke|id|Provinsi Shimotsuke|it|Shimotsuke (provincia)|ja|下野国|ko|시모쓰케국|lt|Šimocukės žemė|nl|Shimotsuke (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimotsuke|ru|Симоцукэ (провинция)|simple|Shimotsuke Province|sk|Šimocuke (provincia)|sr|Провинција Шимоцуке|tr|Shimotsuke (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоцуке|zh|下野國|zh_min_nan|Simotuke-kok|zh_yue|下野國|qid=Q1053699}}, listed in the 『{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}』, though there are differing opinions. One theory holds that the Arakashi Shrine was enshrined together as an auxiliary shrine at {{ill|Ōsaki Shrine|Q11433065|qid=Q11433065}}<ref>“Tochigi Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer,” p. 41</ref>. As a Shikinaisha, it is said to have been ranked fifth among the eleven shrines of Shimotsuke Province<ref name="#1">“Tochigi Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer,” p. 700</ref>. The enshrined deities are {{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Q478504|qid=Q478504|lt=Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kunisatsuchi-no-Mikoto|ja|国狭槌尊|ru|Куни сацути-но микото|uk|Куні но сацуті но мікото|zh|國狹槌尊|qid=Q5966692}}, and {{ill|Toyokumono-no-Mikoto|es|Toyo-kumo-no-no-kami|ja|トヨクモノ|ru|Тоё-кумоно-но ками|uk|Тойо кумоно но камі|zh|豐斟渟尊|qid=Q4387158|lt=Toyokumonunu-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="#1"/>.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the first year of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}})<ref name="#1"/>. It stands atop Mount Takafuji, northeast of Kikyo Castle ({{ill|Motegi Castle|Q11617091|qid=Q11617091}}), and is said to have been established to protect the castle from the demon’s gate (northeast)<ref name="#1"/>.  In the 6th year of {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} ({{ill|1721|Q6913|qid=Q6913}}), with the support of the {{ill|Hosokawa clan|Q2736120|qid=Q2736120}}, who ruled the area, the shrine buildings were rebuilt<ref name="#1"/>. In the 4th year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), it became a Motegi Domain shrine, and in the 13th year of {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} ({{ill|1938|Q18645|qid=Q18645}}), it was promoted to Prefectural Shrine rank<ref name="#1"/>. Prior to this, the shrine buildings were reconstructed from Shōwa 9 to 11<ref name="#1"/>.

The precincts overlook the town center of Motegi and are covered with ancient cedar, zelkova, and oak trees estimated to be around 1,000 years old, within which the shrine buildings stand<ref name="#1"/>. In {{ill|2018|Q25291|qid=Q25291}}, the shrine served as a filming location for an {{ill|Au (mobile phone company)|Q307110|qid=Q307110|lt=au}} television {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=commercial}} titled “Santaro Series (Half-Price Shop Edition)”<ref>Yomiuri Shimbun, Tochigi edition, January 25, 2018, p. 33.</ref>.

=== Cultural properties ===
A zelkova tree estimated to be 700 years old was designated a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}} of Tochigi Prefecture as of {{ill|January 26|Q2282|qid=Q2282}}, {{ill|1990|Q2064|qid=Q2064}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 2)<ref name="#1"/>.

=== Access ===
A 30-minute walk from {{ill|Motegi Station|Q6917169|qid=Q6917169}} on the {{ill|Mōka Railway|Q11240879|qid=Q11240879}}.
